chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the Mut'a.
So he said: 'Indeed, the Mut'a today is not as it was before today. Indeed, those women were believed (to be valid) at that time, and today they are not believed (to be valid), so ask about them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Mut'a in the past and present according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the permissibility of Mut'a has shifted due to a change in the condition of the women involved; whereas they were previously considered 'believers' (mu'manat) and thus valid for temporary marriage, they are no longer so today. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that the validity of Mut'a is contingent upon the specific religious status of the woman at the time of the contract, rather than being an abrogated ruling entirely. Consequently, the Prophet's instruction to 'ask about them' directs believers to verify the current status of the women in question to determine the ruling's applicability.
